title: Maps from a quasi-coherent module descend from a smooth atlas
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal X/S$ an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $a:U\to\mathcal X$ a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Put $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; $R$ is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space]. On the big fppf ringed site of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], let $G$ be a quasi-coherent module in the local-presentation sense [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and let $H$ be any module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $G_U,H_U$ for their small-etale restrictions [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $G_R,H_R$ for the restrictions along the canonical object of $\mathcal X$ over $R$, interpreted on etale scheme charts. Tensor pullbacks are [def-pc-module-pullback, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $c_i^H:p_i^*H_U\to H_R$ be the canonical tensor comparisons induced by restriction. The analogous maps $c_i^G:p_i^*G_U\to G_R$ are isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], and write $\delta_G=(c_2^G)^{-1}c_1^G$. Restriction gives a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}}(G,H)$ to the set of maps $b:G_U\to H_U$ satisfying $$c_1^H\circ p_1^*b=c_2^H\circ p_2^*b\circ\delta_G.$$ Thus every compatible atlas map extends uniquely to a big-fppf module map. No quasi-coherence or flat-comparison assumption is made on $H$; in particular the maps $c_i^H$ are not assumed invertible. No quasi-compactness, finiteness or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 076S, lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent, for a smooth atlas via Tag 04T5 (algebraic.tex, lemma-stack-presentation). The displayed equation is its commutative comparison diagram.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], every scheme base change of the atlas is a smooth surjective algebraic-space map, whose etale scheme charts are smooth scheme maps. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], these chart maps are flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus $a$ is representable, surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation in the chart-test convention of [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations]. Part (2) of that node supplies the self-relation groupoid $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$, with $s=p_1$, $t=p_2$, flat locally finitely presented projections, and an equivalence $q:[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ commuting with the given atlas. This keeps the actual algebraic space $R$, without replacing it by a scheme.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), applied to algebraic.tex Tags 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation) and 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation).

proof.text: Transfer $G,H$ to $[U/R]$ by precomposition with $q$. Here this transport is formal: an equivalence over $S$-schemes preserves the underlying scheme of each object and arrow, hence the covering families and structure rings of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Precomposition with a quasi-inverse, and the unit and counit evaluated objectwise, give inverse equivalences on module sheaves and their Hom sets. Local presentations by sums of the structure sheaf are unchanged under this identification, so the transferred $G$ is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Because $q$ commutes with the atlas and its canonical self-relation, restrictions and restriction-induced tensor comparisons are identified on every etale scheme chart of $U$ and $R$. Thus the Hom restriction map being studied becomes exactly the restriction map for this quotient presentation.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), applied to algebraic.tex Tags 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation) and 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-groupoid-maps-from-quasicoherent] to this groupoid and the transferred modules $F=G,H$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the quasi-coherence in step 2; its target module is arbitrary. It identifies the Hom set injectively with the atlas maps $b$ for which $$c_1^H\circ p_1^*b\circ(c_1^G)^{-1}=c_2^H\circ p_2^*b\circ(c_2^G)^{-1}:G_R\longrightarrow H_R.$$ It also supplies invertibility of both $G$ comparisons on the algebraic space $R$. Under step 2 these are the comparisons in the question.

source.place: Tag 076S (lemma-map-from-quasi-coherent), applied to algebraic.tex Tags 04T5 (lemma-stack-presentation) and 04WY (remark-flat-fp-presentation).

proof.text: Compose the equality in step 3 on the right with the isomorphism $c_1^G:p_1^*G_U\to G_R$. This yields $$c_1^H\circ p_1^*b=c_2^H\circ p_2^*b\circ(c_2^G)^{-1}\circ c_1^G=c_2^H\circ p_2^*b\circ\delta_G.$$ Conversely composing this equation with $(c_1^G)^{-1}$ recovers the equality of step 3. Therefore the two compatibility subsets coincide. The injectivity and image assertion of step 3, and the Hom identification of step 2, give precisely the claimed bijection and unique extension. Only $G$ comparisons were inverted. The presentation theorem and the groupoid Hom theorem require neither quasi-compactness nor a Deligne--Mumford condition.

lean.statement: theorem smoothAtlas_quasicoherent_source_maps {S : Scheme.{u}} (C : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hC : IsAlgebraicModuliStack C) (U : Over S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) C) (ha : IsSmoothModuliAtlas C U a) (R : AlgebraicSpace S) (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli R.obj.obj) (moduliTwoFiberProduct a a)) (he : e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence) (G H : ringedSiteModules.{max (u + 1) v w} (moduliModuleRings C hC.1.1)) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherent) : Function.Injective ((moduliEtaleChartRestriction hC.1.1 (AlgebraicSpace.schemeSpace U) a).map (X := G) (Y := H)) ∧ ∀ b : (moduliEtaleChartRestriction hC.1.1 (AlgebraicSpace.schemeSpace U) a).obj G ⟶ (moduliEtaleChartRestriction hC.1.1 (AlgebraicSpace.schemeSpace U) a).obj H, (∃ f : G ⟶ H, (moduliEtaleChartRestriction hC.1.1 (AlgebraicSpace.schemeSpace U) a).map f = b) ↔ ModuliAtlasMapCompatible hC.1.1 a R e G H b
lean.note: Canonical restrictions are literal module-presheaf precomposition on the existing small-etale chart sites. Forgetting the sheaf condition is fully faithful. Compatibility is the two canonical tensor comparison squares, expressed on every local section via the tensor/direct-image adjunction, with a common map G_R to H_R; source comparison invertibility gives exactly the displayed delta_G equation. R is an algebraic-space presentation of the actual two-fibre product, never assumed a scheme.
